slot.brief: Given Λm° values of ions by Kohlrausch's law, calculate limiting molar conductivity of a weak electrolyte (e.g., an acid) by linear combination

stem: Given $\text{Λ}_m^\text{°}(\text{HCl})=426$, $\text{Λ}_m^\text{°}(\text{CH}_3\text{COONa})=91$ and $\text{Λ}_m^\text{°}(\text{NaCl})=126$ S cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$, calculate $\text{Λ}_m^\text{°}(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH})$.

verdicts.working: By Kohlrausch’s law: Λ°m(CH₃COOH) = 426 + 91 − 126 = 391 S cm² mol⁻¹.

working:
$\text{Λ}_m^��\text{°}(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH})=\text{Λ}_m^��\text{°}(\text{HCl})+\text{Λ}_m^��\text{°}(\text{CH}_3\text{COONa})-\text{Λ}_m^��\text{°}(\text{NaCl})=426+91-126=391$ S cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$.

Independent check: By Kohlrausch’s law: Λ°m(CH₃COOH) = 426 + 91 − 126 = 391 S cm² mol⁻¹.
solution:
By Kohlrausch’s law of independent migration of ions,
$$\Lambda_m^\circ(\mathrm{CH_3COOH})=\Lambda_m^\circ(\mathrm{HCl})+\Lambda_m^\circ(\mathrm{CH_3COONa})-\Lambda_m^\circ(\mathrm{NaCl})=426+91-126=391\ \text{S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}.$$
